scope: Native forward bit copying for copied public results and construction spans, including disjoint bit ranges sharing a boundary byte. No binary-construction instruction admission or general overlapping copy.
adaptations: erts_copy_bits_fwd and its MAKE_MASK/MASK_BITS macros preserve the native same-byte, aligned memcpy, shifted-byte and masked-tail algorithms. Uint/byte/sys_memcpy use size_t/unsigned char/memcpy; offsets use division and masking by eight.

The original checked boundary rejected touched-byte overlap. The shared-edge follow-on compares normalized byte-address/bit-offset positions after span and address arithmetic checks, allowing logically disjoint bit intervals even when one boundary byte is shared. This covers unaligned append sources without changing the native forward kernel. Its edge masks preserve source bits; aligned memcpy interiors remain byte-disjoint. No pointer is multiplied by eight.

Exact identity is an explicit no-op before entering the native kernel, avoiding C memcpy self-overlap UB. All other overlapping bit intervals, out-of-range offsets/counts, arithmetic overflow and NULL nonempty spans are refused before mutation. Zero-length copies do not dereference either span. Source bits and destination-outside bits survive; unrelated bits in a shared source byte can legitimately be destination bits.

Partial destination bytes must be initialized and retain bits outside the requested interval. Full-byte destinations need no initialization. The native tail read is already conditional on the source bits needed; no allocator padding or extra terminal lookahead is assumed.

Public result transport uses this pure copier after its existing fallible allocation and byte-sized/64-KiB result checks. No scratch, collection, ownership transfer, new BIF or generated instruction is introduced.

The original slice did not supply the later segment/append/error helpers. Those dependencies now exist, but bs_create_bin remains refused pending complete sizing, fixups, ownership proof, virtual-binary-heap policy, work accounting and exception/dispatch integration. Reverse byte-group copying and general overlapping-bit copies remain excluded.

An independent saved-source bit oracle covers both address orders, gaps, exact self-copy, differently based views, true-overlap refusal and long shared-edge copies. Actual C-owned normal/private append builds repeated volatile prefixes, including growth and moving GC; copied results survive source-process retirement. 514 additional stock-OTP vectors compare those compound results, not opcode execution.
